en: I salute Kṛṣṇa, the son of Vasudeva, the God who crushes Kaṃsa and Cāṇūra, the supreme joy of Devakī, and the Teacher of the World. || 1 ||
I bow to Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, who resembles the flax flower, is adorned with necklaces and anklets, and wears jeweled bracelets and armlets. || 2 ||
I bow to Lord Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, who possesses curly locks of hair, whose face resembles the full moon, and who wears shimmering earrings. || 3 ||

I bow to the Teacher of the World, Kṛṣṇa, who is endowed with the fragrance of the Mandāra flower, possesses a beautiful smile, has four arms, and whose head is adorned with a crest of peacock feathers.
I bow to Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world and the crest-jewel of the Yādavas, whose eyes are like the petals of a full-blown lotus and who resembles a dark rain cloud. || 5 ||
I bow to Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, who is beautifully adorned with yellow garments, joined in dalliance with Rukmiṇī, and has acquired the fragrance of tulasī.
I bow to Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, the great archer and abode of Śrī, whose chest is marked with saffron and who is embraced by the pair of breasts of the cowherd girls. 7.
I bow to Lord Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, who bears the Śrīvatsa mark, possesses a broad chest, is resplendent with a forest garland, and holds the conch and the discus. 8.
Whoever, having risen early in the morning, recites this *Kṛṣṇāṣṭaka*,
the sins committed throughout ten million lifetimes are destroyed by its mere remembrance.
May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
